nodes.description: A heterozygous de novo missense substitution in H4C5 changes one residue of histone H4. Because thirteen other genes encode the same protein, and H4 loss-of-function variants occur in healthy people, the variant is thought to act through a dominant effect of the altered protein rather than by reducing the amount of H4.

evidence.reference_title: Recurrent de novo missense variants across multiple histone H4 genes underlie a neurodevelopmental syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Here, we present a cohort of 29 subjects with de novo missense variants in six H4 genes (H4C3, H4C4, H4C5, H4C6, H4C9, and H4C11) identified by whole-exome sequencing and matchmaking.

evidence.reference_title: Recurrent de novo missense variants across multiple histone H4 genes underlie a neurodevelopmental syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Loss-of-function variants in H4 genes are present in the healthy population 17 and are even present in homozygous form, 30 supporting our hypothesis that the variants identified here act through a dominant effect.

genetic_context.description: Heterozygous de novo missense variants. A dominant effect is proposed but a specific functional category has not been demonstrated for H4C5 alleles.

nodes.description: In zebrafish embryos, overexpression of human H4 disease variants caused abnormal general development, head defects, a shortened body axis and tissue necrosis. The H4C5 Arg45Cys variant showed a dose-dependent effect, while Arg40Cys, also an H4C5 allele, had no significant effect. That the human neurodevelopmental and growth features arise from the same disturbance is an inference; no mammalian or human cell model has been reported.
